summary: Volleyball block at the top of the jump: both arms straight and reaching over the net into the opponent's court, hands wide open, shoulders parallel to the net.

environment.text: Net: top tape 2.43 m high, {fwd:net_top:pelvis} cm in front of the hips; fingertips {up:r_fingertip:net_top} cm above the tape and {fwd:r_fingertip:net_top} cm past the net plane into the opponent's court; body stays on its own side.

rules.why: shoulders fully flexed, arms reaching up and forward
hands penetrate past the net plane (about 36 cm in NCAA women)
hands above the tape (about 17 cm in NCAA women; more in men)
body stays on its own side of the net
pelvis and shoulders parallel to the net

text.action: a volleyball blocker at the top of the jump pressing both hands over the net
text.core: Airborne with legs nearly straight and toes pointed down; trunk upright and slightly piked; shoulders square to the net; both arms straight, reaching up and forward over the tape into the opponent's court; hands wide open, fingers spread, palms facing down toward the opponent's floor.
text.gaze: Eyes on the attacker's hitting arm across the net.
cues: penetrate the hands over the net, do not just reach up
pelvis and shoulders parallel to the net
thumbs up, fingers spread and strong
kinetic: net mesh flexing slightly next to the arms
hands firm against an incoming spike
sweat on the forearms catching the arena light
avoid: hands on the blocker's own side
arms spread so wide the ball passes between them

sources.cite: Ficklin et al. 2014, JSSM 13:78: swing vs traditional block (hand penetration 17 cm above and 36.5 cm past the net, NCAA women; search extract)
ISBS blocking paper: pelvis and shoulders parallel to the net, hand penetration
Lobietti, ISBS 2006: block footwork and knee flexion
